title: My Homework
summary: Build a homework tracker with subject cards, an Add Homework form and a saved list.

steps.title: Add the app header
steps.objective: Learn what a header is and how to drag a component onto the phone.
steps.concept: A header is the title bar at the top of an app screen. It tells people where they are, like the title on a book cover.
steps.expected: A navy title bar appears at the top of the phone.

expect.label: A Header sits in the Header zone of My Homework
expect.fail: There is no header on the My Homework screen yet. Drag the Header tool onto the glowing Header zone.

hints: Open the Component Toolbox in the left sidebar. One tool glows gold: Header.
Press and hold the Header tool, then drag it onto the glowing dashed strip at the top of the phone.
Using touch? Tap the Header tool, then tap the glowing Header zone. When the header appears, press Check My Work.

steps.title: Name your screen
steps.objective: Learn that every component has properties you can edit.
steps.concept: Properties are the settings of a component, such as its text. The studio looks after colours and sizes, so you only edit the text.
steps.expected: The header on the phone reads “My Homework”.

expect.label: The header text is exactly My Homework

hints: Click the header on the phone. Its properties appear in the panel on the right.
Find the box labelled Text content in the Properties panel and replace what is inside.
Type exactly: My Homework — capital M, capital H and a space. Then press Check My Work.

steps.title: Add a subject card
steps.objective: Practise dropping a component into the correct zone.
steps.concept: A card is a block that holds one item. We will use one card for each school subject.
steps.expected: A card called “New subject” appears in the body.

expect.label: A Card sits in the Body zone of My Homework
expect.fail: No card yet. Drag the Card tool into the glowing Body zone.

hints: The tool you need is Card. It glows gold in the toolbox.
This time the destination is the Body zone: the big open area in the middle of the phone.
Tap-to-place works too: tap Card, then tap the glowing Body zone.

steps.title: Name the subject with a command
steps.objective: Learn to select a component and change it with a command.
steps.concept: Commands are short instructions you type. SET TEXT changes the text of whatever you have selected. Text always goes inside quotation marks.
steps.expected: The card says Mathematics and the studio gives it a calculator icon.

expect.label: The card text is exactly Mathematics

hints: Commands work on whatever is selected, so click the card on the phone first.
Open the Commands tab in the right panel, click the box and type the command from the step card.
Straight quotation marks go around the text, and Mathematics starts with a capital M. Then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Add another subject
steps.objective: Learn that ADD commands create components in the right zone automatically.
steps.concept: You can build faster by typing. ADD CARD creates a new card and puts it in the Body zone for you.
steps.expected: A second card called Science appears under Mathematics.

expect.label: A card called Science exists
expect.fail: No card called Science yet. Check the quotation marks and the spelling of the command.

hints: ADD CARD makes a new card without any dragging.
Type ADD CARD and then the subject name inside quotation marks.
Exactly: ADD CARD "Science" — then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Add an action button
steps.objective: Learn where buttons live and why.
steps.concept: Buttons let people do things. They sit in the Action bar at the bottom of the screen, where thumbs can reach them.
steps.expected: A gold button appears at the bottom of the phone.

expect.label: A Button sits in the Action bar of My Homework
expect.fail: No button in the Action bar yet. Drag the Button tool to the strip at the bottom of the phone.

hints: Find the glowing Button tool in the toolbox.
Drop it on the glowing strip at the bottom of the phone: the Action bar.
Tap-to-place: tap Button, then tap the Action bar.

steps.title: Label the button
steps.objective: Use the Properties panel again to give a component a clear label.
steps.concept: A good button label says exactly what will happen when you tap it.
steps.expected: The button reads “Add Homework” and the studio picks a plus icon.

expect.label: The button text is exactly Add Homework

hints: Click the button on the phone to select it.
Change Text content in the Properties panel.
Type exactly: Add Homework

steps.title: Move to a new screen
steps.objective: Learn that an app is made of several screens and how to move between them.
steps.concept: Every app has more than one screen. NAVIGATE TO moves the workspace to another screen so you can build it. The names above the phone are the screen names.
steps.expected: The phone switches to the Add Homework screen, which is still empty.

expect.label: You are now on the Add Homework screen
expect.fail: You are still on a different screen. Run the NAVIGATE TO command.

hints: NAVIGATE TO changes which screen you are working on.
The screen name goes in quotation marks and must match the tab names above the phone.
Exactly: NAVIGATE TO "Add Homework"

steps.title: Add a text box
steps.objective: Place an input component on a form.
steps.concept: A text input is a box where people type. On this screen it will collect the title of a homework task.
steps.expected: A text box appears in the middle of the phone.

expect.label: A Text Input sits in the Body zone of Add Homework
expect.fail: No text box yet. Drag the Text Input tool into the Body zone.

hints: You should be on the Add Homework screen. Look for the Text Input tool.
Drop it in the glowing Body zone.
Tap-to-place works too: tap Text Input, then tap the Body zone.

steps.title: Write the hint inside the box
steps.objective: Learn that an input’s text is the hint people see before they type.
steps.concept: A hint inside a box tells people what to type. It disappears once they start typing.
steps.expected: The box shows “Homework title”.

expect.label: The text box hint is exactly Homework title

hints: Click the text box on the phone to select it.
Edit Text content in the Properties panel.
Type exactly: Homework title

steps.title: Add a Save button
steps.objective: Create a button with a command instead of dragging.
steps.concept: ADD BUTTON creates a button in the Action bar. The label you type becomes its text.
steps.expected: A Save button appears in the Action bar of the form.

expect.label: A button called Save is in the Action bar of Add Homework
expect.fail: No Save button on the Add Homework screen yet.

hints: Make sure you are on the Add Homework screen.
ADD BUTTON followed by the label in quotation marks.
Exactly: ADD BUTTON "Save"

steps.title: Make Save do something
steps.objective: Learn that an action tells a button what to do.
steps.concept: Without an action a button does nothing. SAVE HOMEWORK reads the text box on the same screen and stores the text in the browser’s memory (LocalStorage).
steps.expected: The Save button’s linked action shows SAVE HOMEWORK in the Properties panel.

expect.label: The Save button has the action SAVE HOMEWORK
expect.fail: The Save button has no SAVE HOMEWORK action yet.

hints: SET ACTION needs the button label in quotes, then the action name.
The action for this button is SAVE HOMEWORK (two words, no quotes).
Exactly: SET ACTION "Save" SAVE HOMEWORK

steps.title: Link Save to the list
steps.objective: Connect two screens with a link.
steps.concept: A link sends people to another screen after the button’s action finishes. First Save stores the homework, then the app opens the list.
steps.expected: The Save button’s linked action now also says: then go to Homework List.

expect.label: The Save button is linked to Homework List
expect.fail: The Save button is not linked to the Homework List screen yet.

hints: LINK BUTTON has two pieces of text: the button and the screen.
Both names go in quotation marks, with the word TO between them.
Exactly: LINK BUTTON "Save" TO "Homework List"

steps.title: Title the list screen
steps.objective: Use ADD HEADER on a different screen.
steps.concept: Every screen needs a header. The command adds it to the Header zone of the screen you are on.
steps.expected: A “Homework List” header appears at the top of the list screen.

expect.label: The Homework List screen has a header called Homework List
expect.fail: The Homework List screen needs a header with exactly that name.

hints: Check the tab above the phone: you should be on Homework List.
ADD HEADER and the title in quotation marks.
Exactly: ADD HEADER "Homework List"

steps.title: Show saved homework
steps.objective: Place a component that fills itself with saved data.
steps.concept: The Homework List component reads the saved homework and shows it. You do not have to update it by hand.
steps.expected: A list panel appears in the body of the list screen.

expect.label: A Homework List sits in the Body zone of Homework List
expect.fail: No list component on the Homework List screen yet.

hints: Find the Homework List tool in the toolbox.
Drop it in the glowing Body zone.
Tap-to-place: tap Homework List, then tap the Body zone.

steps.title: Open the form from the first screen
steps.objective: Finish the wiring so the whole app is connected.
steps.concept: OPEN FORM tells a button to open the Add Homework screen. The Add Homework button lives on My Homework, so you must go there first. Commands only find components on the screen you are on.
steps.expected: The Add Homework button is linked: tapping it will open the form.

expect.label: The Add Homework button has the action OPEN FORM
expect.fail: The Add Homework button on My Homework has no OPEN FORM action yet. If the console says it can’t find the button, check which screen you are on.

hints: Read the console message if a command fails. It tells you which screen you are on.
First go to My Homework, then set the action. You can type both commands on separate lines.
Line 1: NAVIGATE TO "My Homework"   Line 2: SET ACTION "Add Homework" OPEN FORM

steps.title: Debug a command
steps.objective: Learn to read an error message and fix the mistake.
steps.concept: Bugs are normal, even for professionals. When a command fails, the Console explains what went wrong. Here you will make a mistake on purpose, read the message, then fix it.
steps.expected: The first command fails with a red error about quotation marks. The second one adds a Physics card.

expect.name: quotesSeen
expect.label: You ran a command with a mistake
expect.fail: Run the first command exactly as shown, without quotation marks, so you can see the error.

expect.name: consoleViewed
expect.label: You opened the Console tab to read the error
expect.fail: Open the Console tab in the right panel and read the red message.

expect.name: quotesFixed
expect.label: You fixed it: the Physics card was added
expect.fail: After the error, run the corrected command: ADD CARD "Physics"

subs.t: Type this broken command on purpose:
Read the red error in the Console

hints: Run ADD CARD Physics first. It is meant to fail.
Open the Console tab. The message tells you what is missing around the text.
Fix it by adding quotation marks: ADD CARD "Physics"

steps.title: Look inside: real HTML
steps.objective: See the real HTML code the studio writes for your button.
steps.concept: HTML is the language of web pages. Every component you place becomes an HTML element, written with a tag such as <header> or <article>. The studio writes this for you as you build.
steps.expected: You can name the tag that creates your button.

expect.name: htmlTabViewed
expect.label: You opened the Code tab (HTML/CSS/JavaScript)
expect.fail: Open the Code tab (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) in the right panel.

expect.name: answer
expect.label: Your answer is correct
expect.fail: Not quite. Select the Add Homework button on the phone and look at the gold line in the HTML view. The tag is the first word after <.

subs.t: Click the Add Homework button on the phone
Find the gold line in the Code tab
Type the tag name in the answer box

hints: Click the Code tab, then click the Add Homework button on the phone.
One line in the HTML view turns gold. It starts with a tag name in blue.
The tag name is a single word: the thing you tap.

quiz.prompt: Which HTML tag creates the Add Homework button? (type the tag name)

steps.title: Final style check: every colour, border, shadow and style
steps.objective: Give your screens the same colours, shapes and shadows as the model app.
steps.concept: Colours were chosen while you built each element. Now finish the whole look: every colour, background, border, corner, shadow and text style below must match the model app you tried at the start. Items you already set show a tick.
steps.expected: Your screens look exactly like the model app.
hints: Click the element on the phone first. The style box (Choose colours, borders and corners) opens by itself.
Follow the sub-steps one by one: each says which row to use and which option to click. The red dot shows where.
Text alignment and weight are in the Properties panel (right) under “Text and layout”.

steps.title: Run and test your app
steps.objective: Test your app like a real user and confirm that saved data appears in the list.
steps.concept: Testing means using your app the way a user would. Run Project switches the phone from build mode to a working app.
steps.expected: Your homework title appears on the Homework List screen.

expect.name: ran
expect.label: You pressed Run Project
expect.fail: Press Run Project in the top bar to start your app.

expect.name: saved:homework
expect.label: Homework was saved from the running app
expect.fail: Tap Add Homework, type a title in the box and tap Save inside the running app. If something fails, read the console: it will tell you what is missing.

expect.name: viewed:list:homework
expect.label: You saw it on the Homework List screen
expect.fail: After saving, your app should open the Homework List. If it does not, check the link on the Save button.

subs.t: Press Run Project in the top bar
In the phone, tap Add Homework
Type a homework title in the box:
Look at your homework in the list

hints: Press Run Project. The phone turns into a working app.
Tap Add Homework, type “Read chapter 3”, tap Save.
Nothing happens? Stop the app and check the buttons’ actions in Properties and in Screen Connections in the sidebar.

objectives: Build a form that saves homework with a title.
Show saved homework in a list that updates by itself.
Connect screens with actions and links, and learn to read an error message.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between NAVIGATE TO and LINK BUTTON?
a: NAVIGATE TO moves the screen you are editing; LINK BUTTON sets where a button takes the user
mcqs.why: One moves your workspace, the other builds a connection for users.

mcqs.q: Why are the form and the list on separate screens?
a: Each screen has one clear job
mcqs.why: Single-purpose screens are easier to understand and test.

mcqs.q: An error says a quotation mark is missing. What should you do?
a: Read it, find the mistake, fix it and run again
mcqs.why: Error messages are clues that tell you what to fix.

mcqs.q: Which HTML tag creates a button?
mcqs.why: The studio writes real HTML, where buttons use the button tag.

mcqs.q: Why does an app save data in a collection instead of keeping it on the screen?
a: So it is still there when the user leaves and comes back
mcqs.why: Stored data survives moving between screens.
